purpose: Decide when a solution should adapt model weights instead of prompts or retrieval, and gate every fine-tuning run behind dataset quality, baseline evals, privacy review and human approval.
not_applicable_reason_for_ml: Classical ML training is governed by config/ml_foundations_policy.json; this policy covers LLM, embedding and reranker adaptation.

adaptation_ladder.requires: explicit architecture review and human approval

techniques.sft: supervised fine-tuning on curated input/output pairs
techniques.lora: parameter-efficient adapters; default for open-weight models
techniques.qlora: LoRA on a quantized base model when GPU memory is the constraint
techniques.preference_tuning: DPO-style training on chosen/rejected pairs when ranking quality or tone is the gap
techniques.distillation: train a smaller model on reviewed outputs of a larger model
techniques.embedding_fine_tuning: contrastive pairs (query, relevant chunk) to improve retrieval recall
techniques.reranker_fine_tuning: cross-encoder trained on labeled query/chunk relevance

provider_rules.managed_fine_tuning: Provider-dependent. Confirm supported base models, data retention and pricing with the provider at time of use; do not assume availability.
provider_rules.open_weight_fine_tuning: Allowed on approved local or private infrastructure with PEFT (LoRA/QLoRA).
provider_rules.sensitive_data: Restricted or sensitive datasets never leave the approved environment; cloud fine-tuning requires data classification and human approval.

source_candidates: approved eval failures converted to examples
dataset.split_strategy: deterministic hash of normalized prompt, so the same example never moves between splits

release_gates.baseline: prompt + RAG solution measured on the same eval set
release_gates.rollout: shadow or canary before full traffic
release_gates.rollback: keep base model routing available and switch back on regression
